title: An inbound email claims an issue fixed that never actually closed
author: nisaba
description: The Gmail-side twin of mention-claims-unfixed-issue (the X-mention leg), slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue (the Slack-channel leg), and linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue (the Linear-comment leg) -- and the first recipe under RECIPES/ to name gmail at all, despite SCOPES.md's own Gmail (v0.2) row sitting on the oath table since ROADMAP.md #16 and gmail_calendar.py's own module docstring proposing the toolkit before it had a live scope. Grepped every one of the 92 existing recipes' own recipe.json toolkit field before writing this one: the live set already covers {github, github+x, x+github, slack+github, linear+github, github+google_calendar} -- zero gmail, confirming the gap rather than assuming it. Extracts every real GitHub closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses, the shared seam_engine.closing_keywords grammar fifteen sibling recipes already import) from an inbound email's own body and cross-checks it against the live issue tracker's own state -- a status-update email sitting in an inbox is exactly as durable and readable-later as a tweet, a mention, a Slack message, or a Linear comment, and nothing on either platform ever compares it against the issue tracker's real state. Proposed per CONTRIBUTING.md's own 'New toolkits' section, the exact same way gmail_calendar.py, slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue, and linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue each proposed their own toolkit before it had a live scope -- fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the email's own received_at, holding mention-claims-unfixed-issue's/slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue's/linear-comment-claims-unfixed-issue's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the toolkit is new. A claim checked within 24 hours of the email landing might still be a race (the real fix landing moments after the email went out) rather than a settled overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named issue still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-unfixed-issue sibling: the claimed issue's own live state field, verified against ListIssues, not a guess about which tracker the sender meant. A named issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future email-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. An email with no closing-keyword claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the sender -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
